title: Approve customer-facing free tier + overage copy (usage definitions after meter changes)
creator: Chris Osei
description:
Finalize and approve customer-facing copy for: (1) Free tier and overage behavior, (2) usage definitions (billed vs raw tokens, retries, caching, streaming), and (3) where customers can see/verify usage. This is required to ship meter hardening changes + updated usage API fields without causing disputes or inconsistent Sales messaging.

Background
- We’re introducing clearer “billed_tokens” vs “raw_tokens” semantics and cache-hit attribution in the usage API (PR-27485) and aligning token counting across OpenAI-compatible endpoints (openai-compat PR-511).
- We fixed double-counting on retry/fallback paths (ENG-4430 / PR-27463) and added additional streaming/tool-call tests; copy must not imply customers are charged for failed requests, and must describe how partial streaming completions are handled.
- Pricing experiments in Q1 are sensitive to wording; copy must be consistent across Console, docs, and Sales FAQ.

Owner / approvers
- Product: Nikhil Sharma (final product sign-off)
- Product Marketing/Docs: Soojin Lee (draft + publish)
- Legal: Michael Grant, Sofia Mendes (wording + dispute language)
- Finance/RevRec: Emily Stone (usage definition consistency for invoices), Laura Bennett (material risk visibility)

Deliverables
1) Approved customer-facing copy blocks (below) for:
   - Console plan page (Free tier + overage)
   - Public-ish docs FAQ (Usage & billing)
   - Usage API field definitions (billed_tokens, cache_hit)
2) Final placement plan + owners (where each block lives)
3) Effective date + migration note for customers already using usage exports

Acceptance criteria
- Legal confirms wording does not create audit/inspection obligations beyond contract terms and includes dispute window reference.
- Finance confirms copy aligns with invoice calculation semantics (including idempotency/retry behavior).
- Engineering confirms copy matches actual product behavior in hosted API for streaming, retries, caching attribution, and the usage API schema.
- Sales enablement can link to one canonical explanation of billed vs raw tokens and caching.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Changing pricing rates or packaging thresholds (handled in pricing/packaging docs + exec decisions)
- Contract template updates (tracked separately in Legal playbook)

Final approved customer-facing copy (v5)
A) Free tier (plan page / pricing page)
"Free tier includes a monthly allotment of usage credits. If you exceed your included usage, requests continue to succeed and additional usage is billed at standard overage rates unless you set a hard limit in the Console. You can also configure alerts and spend caps to prevent unexpected charges."

B) Overage + spend controls (Console billing settings)
"Overage billing applies only to usage above your plan’s included allotment. You can:
- set spend caps (hard stop) or soft limits (alerts)
- review daily usage and download exports
- see billed usage by model, region, and project"

C) Usage definition: billed tokens (docs FAQ + Console tooltip)
"Redwood bills for tokens processed to serve your request. Your usage details may show both:
- Raw tokens: tokens observed in the request/response payloads
- Billed tokens: tokens counted by Redwood’s metering system for billing

In most cases, raw tokens and billed tokens match. Differences can occur due to caching (served from cache), internal retries/fallbacks (not double-charged), or partial streaming completion."

D) Caching (docs FAQ)
"If a response (or a portion of a response) is served from cache, Redwood attributes a cache hit in usage details. Cached portions are not billed as newly generated tokens."

E) Retries, timeouts, and fallback (docs FAQ)
"Redwood is designed to be reliable under transient failures. If we retry or route to a compatible fallback internally, we do not double-charge the same request. If your client retries a request, each successfully processed request may be billed; use idempotency keys to avoid unintended duplicate charges."

F) Streaming (docs FAQ)
"For streaming responses, usage is based on tokens actually produced and delivered. If a streaming connection is interrupted, you may see billed tokens for content that was generated and sent before the disconnect."

G) Tool/function calling + structured outputs (docs FAQ)
"When using tool/function calling or structured outputs, tokens are billed based on the underlying model processing required to produce the output (including any tool-call formatting that the model generates). Usage details will still break down prompt vs completion tokens where available."

H) Where to verify usage (docs FAQ + Console)
"You can review usage in the Redwood Console and via the Usage API. Usage exports are available daily. Invoices are calculated from billed usage. If you believe there is an error, contact Support within the dispute window in your agreement and include the account, date range, and usage export."

I) Dispute / support language (docs FAQ; aligned with Legal)
"If you believe your invoice does not reflect your billed usage, please contact Support with the relevant export(s). We’ll investigate and, where appropriate, apply credits or adjustments consistent with your agreement."

Implementation notes (where this copy lands)
- Docs: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-642-update-usage-and-billing-faq.json
  - Adds sections C–I to the Usage & Billing FAQ
- Console:
  - Plan page: A
  - Billing settings: B + short links to FAQ
  - Usage table tooltips: C (shortened), D (tooltip)
- Usage API docs / SDK docs:
  - Field definitions for billed_tokens + cache_hit (PR-27485)
- Sales enablement:
  - PM-1860 will link to this canonical wording; do not paraphrase “retries/fallback” language

Open questions resolved in this ticket
- Q: Are customers ever billed for internal retries?
  - A: No; copy explicitly states we do not double-charge internal retries/fallbacks. (Validated with Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman; fix tracked in ENG-4430.)
- Q: For streaming disconnects, do we bill for tokens generated but not received?
  - A: We bill for tokens generated and sent before disconnect; copy says “generated and sent”.
- Q: Do we claim caching always reduces billed tokens?
  - A: We say cached portions are not billed as newly generated tokens and usage details will indicate a cache hit; avoids over-promising while matching attribution behavior.

Rollout / effective date
- Effective date for updated copy: 2026-03-03 (coordinated with docs publish + Console text update)
- Customer comms: No proactive email blast; Sales/Support will use updated FAQ for any inbound questions. For customers in active procurement, AEs may attach the FAQ link.

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: Copy implies contract-level guarantees (audit rights, refunds).
  - Mitigation: Legal-approved language; dispute handling phrased as “consistent with your agreement.”
- Risk: Meter changes overlap with pricing experiments and could be used as “gotcha” in sales calls.
  - Mitigation: Keep messaging consistent with billed vs raw tokens; Sales FAQ uses the same phrasing and points to one canonical doc.
